ashley: ran a prolonged long-context soak (45m, seq 12k variable) and saw steady RSS creep + sporadic p95 token latency spikes during reclaim windows. collecting notes.

mike: what's the repro and the symptom timeline?

ashley: repro: `tests/kv/soak_long_context.sh --pods 32 --seq 12000 --dur 2700`
ashley: observed: baseline p95 ~11ms -> intermittent spikes up to 250ms correlated with reclaim bursts; node RSS climbed ~22% over 45m; allocator small-alloc counter steadily rising.

tara: any recent changes touching reinserts or timestamping logic?

ashley: we recently merged the probation-map refactor (2w ago) but no direct changes to pager. profiler points heavy CPU in `evicter::reinsert` and `kv_pager::page_out`.

zach: can you paste pprof top output?

ashley: pprof top snippet:
```
46.8%  evicter::reinsert
21.4%  kv_pager::page_out
9.1%   allocator::alloc_small
7.3%   scheduler::wake
```

priya: reinsert work doing lots of reuse_score math + list churn could explain fragmenting allocator behavior.

mike: did you capture allocator histograms and slab utilization?

ashley: yes. small allocation rate up ~2.8x, fragmentation ratio (rss/used) drifted 1.10 -> 1.38. many tiny frees not getting coalesced.

zach: any clues in timestamp handling? reinserts rely on `last_seen` ordering right?

ashley: found usage where we store `now = rdtsc_rel()` on different threads and later compare. rdtsc_rel on some hosts shows occasional backward jumps when vcpu migrates.

mike: so comparator can see non-monotonic last_seen, causing entries to appear "older" than they really are -> reinserts reorder badly.

tara: that would cause hot entries to be evicted then quickly reinserted, thrashing the pager and allocator.

priya: quick mitigation ideas?

zach: options: 1) clamp timestamps on compare, 2) use per-shard monotonic incrementing reuse counter, 3) switch to kernel CLOCK_MONOTONIC consistent source.

ashley: implemented a per-evicter-shard atomic incrementing reuse_id and attach on reinsert instead of raw timestamp. local 30m run shows reinserts down ~55% and reinsert CPU time reduced ~43%.

mike: what about latency and memory?

ashley: p95 reduced from 250ms->60ms in stress; RSS growth stabilized (fragmentation ratio ~1.12). small alloc rate normalized to ~1.05x baseline.

tara: good. still need to root-cause the time source skew. what caused rdtsc_rel jumps? host vcpu migrations or hypervisor TSC sync.

ashley: infra will follow up; opened infra ticket to audit TSC handling on affected fleet.

zach: add invariant tests: fuzzed comparator with backward timestamps and ensure eviction order stable. Also add unit that simulates rapid reinsert churn with per-shard counter.

ashley: added two unit tests and a fuzz harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evicter/pull/412

priya: add metrics and alerts: `kv.reinserts.rate`, `kv.pager.thrash.rate`. Alert if reinserts > 150/min sustained for 5m or pager thrash > 40/min.

ashley: added dashboard (kv -> paging) and alert rule. planning staged canary rollout to dedicated clusters (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

mike: double-check probation-map refactor for missed atomics too.

ashley: yes i'm auditing that now. also scheduling a 2h poke run across prod-like canaries tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

ci-bot: build #evicter/412 passed (linux-x86_64, perf=ok)

ashley: merging hotfix branch after one more canary pass. will post a short postmortem if this shows up in prod. ping me if you want to join the repro run :thumbsup:
